title: UDLF deployment config — Splunk via contentctl-ng
description: Config for `platform: splunk-contentctl-ng`. Emits an ESCU 6.x detection for the contentctl-ng pipeline. `type` drives the findings matrix. Closed, and weight is `score`, not severity.

then.$comment: TTP and Correlation both raise a direct alert, so contentctl-ng requires a finding block (action.notable). The difference between them is what else they emit — see the intermediate_findings rules below.
Anomaly contributes risk without alerting directly, and Hunting neither alerts nor scores, so neither may carry a finding. contentctl-ng rejects the block outright rather than ignoring it.
An Anomaly detection's only output is risk contribution, so intermediate_findings is mandatory — without it the detection would emit nothing at all.
A Correlation fires on risk that other detections have already contributed, so contributing more would be circular; a Hunting detection scores nothing. contentctl-ng forbids the block on both.

Threat objects are serialised into action.risk.param._risk, which a Hunting detection never emits. Upstream models this as 'must be empty' rather than 'must be absent', so an explicit empty list stays legal.

allOf.$comment: Exactly one of the two may be defined. Neither is required — omitting both selects the content pack's default schedule — but declaring both is contradictory and contentctl-ng rejects it.

schema.description: Sub-schema revision this block was authored against, e.g. `splunk-contentctl-ng::0.1.0`. The platform name carries no version, so this pin is the only format statement.

type.description: contentctl-ng analytic type, the discriminator. TTP = finding + optional intermediate findings; Anomaly = intermediate only; Correlation = finding only; Hunting = neither.

category.description: Detection category, required by contentctl-ng. Prefer the value matching the telemetry the search reads.

security_domain.description: ES security domain the detection belongs to.

asset_type.description: Type of asset the detection targets. A closed list, and not the same one `splunk-contentctl-v5-6` accepts.

data_source.description: Data sources this detection relies on, resolving under the pack's `data_sources/`. May be empty. Join several with ` AND `.

product.description: Splunk products the detection is valid for. contentctl-ng requires all three, so omit and let the deployer emit the triple.

schedule.description: Name of a schedule under the pack's `schedules/`. Mutually exclusive with `custom_schedule`; omit both for the pack default.

custom_schedule.description: Inline schedule, when this detection needs different timing from the rest of the pack. Mutually exclusive with `schedule`; all four keys required.

cron_schedule.description: Cron expression for the saved search. Unconstrained here, since upstream validates it with a function rather than a pattern.

schedule_window.description: How far the scheduler may delay the search. `auto`, or an integer number of minutes.

earliest_time.description: Start of the search window. A narrow subset of Splunk time syntax: a signed offset with an optional snap.

latest_time.description: End of the search window, under the same narrow syntax as `earliest_time`.

finding.description: The detection's primary alert, as an ES8 Finding. Enables `action.notable`. Required for TTP and Correlation, forbidden for Anomaly and Hunting.

title.description: Finding title, serialised to `action.notable.param.rule_title`. Supports `$field$` substitution.
examples: A download cradle was executed on $dest$ by $user$

entity.description: The single subject the finding is attributed to. Exactly one; further scored entities belong in `intermediate_findings`.

field.description: Search field holding the entity (`risk_object_field`). Must be present in the search.

score.description: Risk contributed each time the detection fires (`risk_score`). Where alert weight is expressed on this platform. No upper bound; 0 raises the finding without contributing risk.

intermediate_findings.description: Risk-contributing entities that raise no direct alert, as ES8 Intermediate Findings. Required for Anomaly, optional for TTP, forbidden for Correlation and Hunting.

entities.description: The scored entities. At least one is required whenever the block is present.

field.description: Search field holding the entity (`risk_object_field`). Must be present in the search.

score.description: Risk contributed by this entity each time the detection fires (`risk_score`). No upper bound.

message.description: Risk message for this entity, supporting `$field$` substitution. Required on every entity.
examples: A download cradle was executed on $dest$

threat_objects.description: Indicators associated with the detection. Permitted for TTP, Anomaly and Correlation; must be empty for Hunting. Entries must be unique.

field.description: Search field holding the threat object. Must be present in the search.

type.description: Category of the threat object. A closed list enforced at build time, with no `other` fallback. Differs from the Splunk RBA list; do not rewrite between them.

drilldown_searches.description: Drilldown searches surfaced with the alert. Omit to let the build generate defaults from the finding and intermediate-finding entities.

search.description: Drilldown SPL. May contain `%original_detection_search%`, substituted at build time.

earliest_offset.description: Start of the drilldown window. Required explicitly, with no default. Commonly `$info_min_time$`.

latest_offset.description: End of the drilldown window. Required explicitly, with no default. Commonly `$info_max_time$`.

baselines.description: Baseline objects this detection depends on, each under the pack's `baselines/`.

atomic_guid.description: Atomic Red Team test GUIDs this detection covers. Distinct from the UDLF `tests` array.
